subject: What's on in E2 · 15–21 October: a free Sebright bill and a big Saturday
preheader: A free three-band bill at the Sebright, free karaoke, a Saturday at the Working Men's Club and house on Brick Lane.

paragraphs: This is the first Bethnal Green Live. I live round here, and I wanted something like my friend Cat's Peckham Live newsletter for E2, so I started one: a short note every Thursday on what's on nearby.
A word on how it's made. The listings are found by AI and checked word for word against each venue's or ticket seller's own page, and I read every issue before it goes out.

It's a slim first week, nearly all gigs and club nights. I'd start with Thursday's free three-band bill in the Sebright's basement, and keep Saturday in mind for the Working Men's Club, where the night runs till 2am.

items.blurb: A free three-band bill of dream punk, post punk and grunge in the Sebright's basement gig room. For the price, an easy yes.

sections.heading: Saturday, two ways
sections.lede: Two very different Saturday nights: one local, one a short walk out.

items.headline: Chudahye Chagis live at Rich Mix
items.blurb: A gig from Chudahye Chagis, whose sound is listed as psychedelic shamanic funk. Rich Mix is an arts centre, so it makes a change from the usual pub back room.

items.headline: Margo Marshall at the Working Men's Club
items.blurb: A late club night at Bethnal Green Working Men's Club, with Margo Marshall billed and the night running from 9pm to 2am. As local as it gets.
A free late-night sing-song at the Sebright, on Friday nights from 10pm.
A multi-act Monday bill at the Sebright for £6: a cheap, early-in-the-week reason to go out.

notes_for_fred: Thin first issue: 8 of the week's 9 events used, all nights and music. No arts, food or community listings this week, so those sections are left out rather than padded.

The pick is a free Thursday gig on the day the email goes out. If you would rather lead with a Saturday, the Working Men's Club night (BRAT 2 SCHOOL, 9pm-2am, £8-£12) is the alternative, but its record has little detail beyond one billed name.
The three 93 Feet East events have no price in the record, so they are compact lines with no blurb and nothing about cost.
Melio Records and TRMNL (both Saturday house at 93 Feet East) are near-identical and sit next to each other in More on Brick Lane. I kept both to reach a three-item section; drop one if you prefer.
COWZ at the Sebright (Friday, price not listed) was left out to keep the Sebright to three events.
